rounds.text: Ansal Buildwell Ltd trades at a highly compelling valuation, sitting at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.48x against a book value of 176 per share [E2], representing a deep discount compared to the broader sector benchmark price-to-book ratio of 5.67x [E7]. This low valuation is starkly decoupled from recent operational acceleration, highlighted by trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 22% [E17], a 212% surge in compounded profit growth over the same period [E21], and screen-noted year-over-year profit growth reaching 292% [E61]. Furthermore, profits are fully backed by cash, evidenced by a robust cash conversion ratio of 1.46x alongside positive operating cash flow of Rs 1.18 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 1.00 Cr in Mar 2026 [E34, E35, E36]. The business also maintains moderate leverage with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.38x and stable promoter holding of 54.83% [E37, E41], while the insider-bias checklist explicitly notes that results are rapidly improving with a results score of 98/100, warning against dismissing a fundamental turnaround based on stale sentiment [E64]. Conceded: [E14, E18, E44, E56].

Ansal Buildwell Ltd carries severe fundamental vulnerabilities that undermine its seemingly attractive low price-to-book ratio [E2, E7]. Long-term top-line erosion is glaring, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of -8% and a 5-year rate of -11% [E14, E15], accompanied by a 10-year compounded profit growth of -20% [E18]. Profitability metrics are exceptionally weak, highlighted by a 3-year median return on equity of just 6% and a dismal 1% over the last year [E28, E29]. Operating margins show a deteriorating structural trend, collapsing by 30 percentage points in TTM compared to three years prior [E30] alongside a four-year yearly operating-margin trend that reads decreasing [E32]. Furthermore, the business suffers from rising borrowings, which climbed to Rs 49.31 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 42.04 Cr previously [E39], coupled with negative warning flags such as a low interest coverage ratio [E53], heavy contingent liabilities of Rs 38.0 Cr [E56], and earnings flattered by Rs 4.29 Cr in other income [E57]. Valuation-wise, a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 73 per share, leaving a negative margin of safety of -16.3% against the market price of Rs 85.3 [E44, E45], while the dividend yield sits entirely at 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: the company demonstrates recent top-line and bottom-line acceleration with a 22% TTM sales growth and a 212% TTM profit growth, alongside cash conversion backing profits fully at 1.46x [E17, E21, E34].

Conceded: [E14], [E15], [E18], [E28], [E29], [E30], [E32], [E39], [E44], [E45], [E53], [E56], and [E57]. However, the bear's gloomy historical focus completely ignores an explosive operational turnaround that renders stale sentiment irrelevant [E64]. Trailing twelve-month sales growth has rebounded to 22% [E17], supported by recent quarterly metrics displaying massive year-over-year surges of +78% in sales and +292% in net profit [E59, E61]. Compounded profit growth over the last three years has reached 32% [E20], culminating in a staggering 212% profit expansion in the trailing twelve months [E21]. This massive acceleration is entirely backed by real cash generation, demonstrated by a 1.46x cash conversion ratio delivering Rs 1.00 Cr in free cash flow [E34, E36]. Meanwhile, the stock trades at deeply discounted multiples, including a P/E of 13x to 14.27x against a sector benchmark of 40.5x [E1, E6], and a price-to-book ratio of just 0.48x compared to a lofty sector average of 5.67x [E2, E7].
